title: Inverse-Modulus Inference for Population-Optimal Trimming under Curvature Loss
banked_reason: D0.5.G achieved only incremental novelty below the fixed field floor; the score ceiling was 6.4 < 7.4 and no bounded in-scope repair could lift the tier.
gap_reasons: The note proves a matched inverse-modulus risk and honest expected-diameter result on one explicit ordered Gaussian causal class, and its framing correctly confines sharpness to that class.

The class assumes a global signed-well inequality that already supplies the cubic restoring shape; the observational theorem proves an upper transfer conditional on known nuisance-rate envelopes, not a matching observational frontier.

The general continuation theorem likewise requires a shared surface chart, a positive profiled quartic coefficient, a global objective gap, and a derivative perturbation bound rather than deriving those conditions from causal-law primitives.

The tie certificate proves coverage and objective-gap exclusion on a bounded two-component design, but establishes no useful effect-diameter rate, and the package gives no application showing the value of selecting populations by this criterion.

At allowed endpoint roots, empirical rank centers can fall just outside [x_{3/8},x_{5/8}], while a_loc controls only centers inside it; no boundary-neighborhood/translation bound for E|K_ell(hat x_p-X)|R_q is given, so (7)--(8) and the uniform rate do not follow.
D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.4 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'incremental'.
proof_attempt_summary: The run developed a same-class Gaussian inverse-modulus upper/lower frontier with honest expected-diameter control, constrained surface continuation, a zero-multiplier square-root witness, an observational cross-fitted upper transfer, and finite-grid certification through global ties. The general referee assessed the delivered contribution as incremental and unsalvageable to field within scope; moreover, the observational proof retains a bounded empirical-center/local-bias gap, while the remaining panel findings are removable restrictions or positioning defects. A future retry should first close that soundness gap, then re-anchor around a genuinely new matched observational lower frontier, primitive causal-law continuation geometry, or rate-sharp tie-effect inference rather than rerunning the present package.
tldr: The fixed-set causal precision optimizer has a rank-two surface curvature diagnostic and a sharp inverse-modulus inference frontier on the explicit randomized Gaussian class. A cross-fitted ordered observational extension now gives an honest upper transfer bound: primitive local and integrated nuisance products add to the boundary information scale, and effect projection adds its integrated error. The result preserves the randomized oracle rate when those products are of order \(r_n\); it does not claim a matching slower observational lower bound. The selected effect remains distinct from the fixed-set variance criterion, and a separate global profile certificate covers genuine optimizer ties.
gap: Precision trimming and convex-minimizer theory do not yet supply a verified same-class causal variance-score frontier when the fixed-set precision optimizer loses curvature, nor a criterion-specific complete effect set at ties. General minimizer adaptation and honest expected-length intervals are established by Cai, Chen and Zhu (2023; revised 2024).
fill: Establish regular-surface and KKT geometry, prove a fixed-constant same-class Gaussian inverse-modulus frontier with causal likelihood lower pairs and honest expected diameter, and determine observational nuisance and tied-branch conditions for outer inference.
